messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: Spike detected - gpu_queue_length > 500 in us-west2 spot pools for the last 6m. Priority: P1. Routing to #incidents and paging @oncall.

Maria (oncall): seeing this now. queue length jumped at ~18:03 UTC. requests are backing up, latency for hosted-api is > 3s 95th. Paging infra.

Kevin: thanks Maria. any obvious autoscaler errors?

Maria (oncall): checking controller logs. quick grep shows a bunch of: 
```
ERROR autoscaler: scaleUp failed: quotaExceeded: "Requested GPUs exceed quota"
WARN autoscaler: fallback attempt to dedicated failed: no compatible nodes available
```

Anita: hmm quotaExceeded on us-west2? that sounds like cloud project quota exhausted, not our autoscaler bug. Could be multiple large customers spiking.

Jules (eng-infra): I'm on it. grabbing metrics from K8s and our pool allocation. Also checking spot eviction rates.

SRE Bridge: @Jules please confirm whether nodepool autoscaler disabled scale-to-zero or hit max nodes. We need to know if it's a config cap or cloud-side quota.

Jules (eng-infra): quick snapshot: 
- pool: us-west2-spot-gpu-pool-a
- desired: 120 nodes, current: 118 nodes, max: 120 nodes (autoscaler max reached)
- spot eviction rate: 7% over 10m
- queue growth: 520 -> 980 in 12m

Maria (oncall): so autoscaler hit max nodes. that's why scaleUp fails even though cloud quota maybe available? but logs had quotaExceeded too. two independent constraints.

Anita: possibility: cluster autoscaler max was set conservatively earlier to limit cost. We must decide: raise max nodes or trigger fallback routing to Dedicated. Which is quicker?

Kevin: raising max nodes requires a short config change (1-2min) and then cloud quota check. Fallback routing needs model compatibility check and warming dedicated pools, could take longer.

Jules (eng-infra): I'm proposing a two-pronged approach: 1) temporarily increase autoscaler max from 120 -> 220 to allow immediate scale; 2) simultaneously request emergency quota bump with cloud support (I've opened the ticket). Also, enable route-split to direct new requests to reserved-dedicated for high-latency sensitive customers.

Maria (oncall): +1. take it, Jules. I'm going to annotate incident timeline and inform CS for customer-facing updates.

deploy-bot: NOTE: change requested by jules to kube autoscaler config: set maxNodes=220 in us-west2-spot-gpu-pool-a. Approval needed from oncall.

Maria (oncall): approved. deploy.

Jules (eng-infra): applying now. patch: 
```yaml
- name: us-west2-spot-gpu-pool-a
  autoscaler:
    min: 10
    max: 220
```
Applying...

Jules (eng-infra): patch applied. cluster autoscaler acknowledged new max. starting scale-up.

SRE Bridge: any sign of nodes joining?

Jules (eng-infra): nodes coming up but we're getting a few provisioning errors: 
```
Event: NodeCreationFailed: API rate limit exceeded when creating VMs
```
So cloud side rate limits also throttling. opening parallel ticket with cloud infra.

Anita: if cloud rate limits are in play, we should stagger instance creation and also check fallback pools in other regions. Could move non-low-latency tenants to us-west1 or eu-west temporarily.

CS - Lina: we have two mid-market customers complaining about increased latencies on embeddings jobs. Can we provide ETA for mitigation?

Maria (oncall): ETA: node bootstrap + queue drain ~20-30m if provisioning continues. I'm escalating for priority quota/rate-limit support. I'll send CS a 30m update now.

Kevin: in parallel, we should enable request-level throttling for best-effort workloads to reduce queue pressure. Recommend applying temporary policy to cap long-run batch jobs.

Jules (eng-infra): adding a temporary limiter on batch-route: set concurrency=4 and max_tokens_per_minute=50000 for batch endpoint. Patching now.

Maria (oncall): patch deployed. seeing backlog growth slow from +40/s to +12/s. good sign.

incident-bot: Incident annotated: reason=autoscaler_max_hit + cloud_rate_limit + spot_evictions. severity=P1.

Jules (eng-infra): cloud support responded: quota bump approved but manual review needed in 25m. rate-limit window is 1m, suggests we wait then retry provisioning.

Anita: plan B now: if nodes don't arrive in 30m, we should failover hot customers to dedicated pools and enable model-approx variants to reduce GPU memory per shard. Also consider temporarily reducing model max_sequence to trim memory.

Maria (oncall): ordering: 1) wait 10m for provisioning to catch up, 2) if not improved, execute dedicated routing for top-tier customers, 3) begin model approx/seq limit changes as last resort.

CS - Lina: please prepare a short customer message: "We're experiencing higher latencies due to GPU capacity; we're scaling and expect service normalization within 30 minutes; we will post updates every 30 minutes." I can send to affected accounts once we have 30m ETA.

Kevin: I also recommend we flag billing not to charge retries for affected customers for this window — coordinate with finance after stabilization.

Jules (eng-infra): update: new nodes are joining 14/100 within 6m. queue rate now +6/s. provisioning still throttled but improving.

Maria (oncall): good. keep monitoring. I'll handoff to overnight oncall at 20:00 UTC if not resolved. current plan remains in effect.

deploy-bot: Rollout: temporary batch limiter was deployed to production (batch-route).

Anita: note for postmortem: autoscaler max was set low in the last cost-control change. We should add a safety policy that automatically raises max during sustained queue growth before human approval.

Jules (eng-infra): noted. I've also scheduled a hotfix to improve our provision retries with exponential backoff to avoid hitting cloud rate-limits.

SRE Bridge: assigning postmortem owners: Jules (lead), Anita (root cause), Maria (timeline and customer comms), Kevin (mitigation policy).

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: queue length 980 -> 420 in 28m. Impact: elevated latencies for batch/embedding endpoints; a subset of dedicated customers routed as fallback. Next update in 30m or on significant change.

CS - Lina: sent initial customer notification to affected accounts. responses are calm for now. will escalate if any SLA violations.

Maria (oncall): handoff note for night oncall: keep monitoring node join rate, queue length, and customer escalations. if queue > 600 for 30m, enact dedicated failover for top-10 customers. contact Jules & Anita for infra changes.

Kevin: thanks team. summary for post-incident: root causes: conservative autoscaler max + spot evictions + cloud provisioning rate limits. mitigation: raised max, throttled batch, requested quota bump, staged dedicated routing.

Jules (eng-infra): closing the active mitigation loop. will follow up with a detailed postmortem doc in #postmortems once we stabilize.

Maria (oncall): incident transitioning to monitoring. I'll close the on-call bridge in 45m if metrics remain steady. :white_check_mark:
